groups.name: Sinaloa Cartel
groups.summary: Mexico's oldest major trafficking federation, now split by war between the Chapitos (sons of El Chapo) and the Mayiza (El Mayo Zambada's faction) since Sept 2024.
groups.says_vs_does: Its leaders long cultivated a 'no fentanyl' image. In practice the DEA names Sinaloa a top fentanyl producer, and Treasury keeps sanctioning its suppliers.

leaders.name: Ismael 'El Mayo' Zambada
leaders.status: Sentenced to life in the US, Jul 2026

groups.name: Los Chapitos
groups.summary: Faction led by El Chapo's sons. They are fighting the Mayiza for Culiacán, Mazatlán and the sierra.
groups.says_vs_does: They publicly deny handing El Mayo to the US, but his July 2024 abduction by Joaquín Guzmán López set off the war.

groups.name: La Mayiza
groups.summary: Faction loyal to El Mayo Zambada, now without him. Mexico charged figures from both factions in Oct 2026.

groups.name: Jalisco Cartel New Generation (CJNG)
groups.summary: Expansive, militarised cartel. The DEA says it is present in more than 40 countries. Its founder El Mencho was killed on 22 Feb 2026, and succession is unconfirmed.
groups.says_vs_does: The reports name Juan Carlos Valencia 'El Pelón' as the likely successor. InSight Crime warns this is not confirmed.

groups.name: Gulf Cartel
groups.summary: Fragmented Tamaulipas cartel. Its old armed wing, the Zetas, split off in 2010.

groups.name: Cartel del Noreste
groups.summary: Zetas successor group controlling Nuevo Laredo.

groups.name: La Nueva Familia Michoacana
groups.summary: Operates in Guerrero, Michoacán and the State of Mexico.

groups.name: Cárteles Unidos
groups.summary: Michoacán coalition formed against the CJNG.

groups.name: Los Viagras
groups.summary: Michoacán group in the Tierra Caliente.

groups.name: Juárez Cartel / La Línea
groups.summary: Controls Ciudad Juárez plazas against Sinaloa-aligned gangs.

groups.name: Tren de Aragua
groups.summary: Venezuelan prison gang that grew into a transnational network of extortion, smuggling and trafficking in people.
groups.says_vs_does: US officials portray it as directed by the Venezuelan state. That claim is contested and still unproven in court.

groups.name: Cartel de los Soles
groups.summary: Label for Venezuelan officials accused of trafficking. Maduro was captured in Jan 2026, and a June 2027 trial start has been proposed.
groups.says_vs_does: InSight Crime describes a loose system of corrupt military networks, not a hierarchical cartel. The US indictment alleges direct leadership.

leaders.name: Nicolás Maduro
leaders.status: In US custody, trial proposed for Jun 2027

groups.name: Clan del Golfo (Urabeños / EGC)
groups.summary: Colombia's largest trafficking group. It controls Urabá and the Darién migrant route.

groups.name: ELN
groups.summary: Marxist guerrilla group active in Colombia and Venezuela. It funds itself through drugs, illegal mining and extortion.
groups.says_vs_does: It presents itself as a political insurgency, but its operations depend on criminal economies on both sides of the border.

groups.name: Segunda Marquetalia
groups.summary: FARC dissidents who rearmed in 2019.

groups.name: Los Choneros
groups.summary: Ecuadorian prison gang linked to Sinaloa. Its leader Fito escaped in 2024, was recaptured in 2025 and was extradited to the US.

leaders.name: José Adolfo 'Fito' Macías
leaders.status: Extradited to the US Jul 2025; pleaded not guilty

groups.name: Los Lobos
groups.summary: Ecuador's largest gang, tied to the CJNG. Also active in illegal gold mining.

groups.name: PCC (Primeiro Comando da Capital)
groups.summary: Brazil's most powerful criminal organisation. It dominates the cocaine trade through Santos.

groups.name: Comando Vermelho
groups.summary: Rio de Janeiro faction expanding in the Amazon.

groups.name: MS-13
groups.summary: Transnational gang weakened in El Salvador by mass detention under the state of exception.

groups.name: Barrio 18
groups.summary: MS-13's main rival in Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador.

groups.name: Chinese money laundering networks
groups.summary: Brokers who swap cartel dollars for pesos through mirror transactions. Not designated as a group.

groups.name: Los Tiguerones
groups.summary: Designated as an FTO. This v1 has no further profile.

groups.name: Chone Killers
groups.summary: Designated as an FTO. This v1 has no further profile.

groups.name: Viv Ansanm (Haiti)
groups.summary: Designated as an FTO. This v1 has no further profile.

groups.name: Gran Grif (Haiti)
groups.summary: Designated as an FTO. This v1 has no further profile.

edges.text: Open war since Sept 2024, after El Mayo's abduction to the US.
Zetas split from the Gulf Cartel in 2010.
Alleged by the US government. Contested and unproven in court.
Alleged sanctuary and cocaine ties, per US charges.

note: Alliances are fluid and often reported by a single source. Alleged state links are allegations unless a court has decided them.
